  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  March 4, 2024

Chair Knieling called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. in the Council Chambers,
Norwalk City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to the roll
call were, Commissioner Fernandez-Silva, Commissioner Greenidge, Commissioner
Hoskins, Chair Knieling, Commissioner LeGaspi, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez,
Commissioner Rosoff. Also present were Ozzie Ramos, Director of Public Safety,
Berenia Orozco, Management Analyst, Richard Newton, Office of Emergency Manager,
and Dolores Bustamante, Code Compliance Supervisor.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Chair Knieling called for the approval of the Public Safety commission meeting minutes
that was held on November 6, 2023. Commissioner LeGaspi seconded the motion. The
minutes were approved. Berenia Orozco recorded the motion of approval.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Commissioner  Fernandez-Silva,  Commissioner  Greenidge,
  Commissioner Hoskins, Chair Knieling, Commissioner LeGaspi,
  Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Commissioner Rosoff
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Commissioner Heard, Vice Chair Pena
ABSTAIN:

REPORTS

Mrs. Orozco called for the reorganization of the Chair and Vice Chair. Commissioner
Hoskins nominated Commissioner Greenidge for the position of Chair. Chair Knieling
seconded the motion. The motion was approved, and Mrs. Orozco recorded the motion
of approval.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Commissioner  Fernandez-Silva,  Commissioner Greenidge,
Commissioner Hoskins, Commissioner Knieling, Commissioner LeGaspi,
Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Commissioner Rosoff
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Commissioner Heard, Commissioner Pena
ABSTAIN:
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Norwalk Public Safety Commission
March 4, 2024

Mrs. Orozco asked for a nomination for Vice Chair. The newly appointed Chair
Greenidge nominated Commissioner LeGaspi for the position of Vice Chair.
Commissioner Hoskins seconded the motion. Mrs. Orozco recorded the motion of
approval.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Commissioner Fernandez-Silva, Chair Greenidge, Commissioner
Hoskins, Commissioner Knieling, Commissioner LeGaspi, Commissioner Dr.
Rodriguez, Commissioner Rosoff
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Commissioner Heard, Commissioner Pena
ABSTAIN:

Mrs. Orozco introduced Director of Public Safety, Ozzie Ramos, to present an update
on Public Safety. Mr. Ramos gave his congratulations to the new Chair and Vice Chair
then proceeded to provide an update on department accomplishments for 2023.

Mr. Ramos shared the four divisions within Public Safety which include Field
Operations, Transportation and Security, HOPE, and CSP. He shared that in 2023,
Public Safety Officers responded to over 24,236 calls for service which include
homeless outreach, illegally parked cars, and other quality of life issues. PSO’s assisted
in the recovery of about 122 vehicles, assisted LASD in about 385 traffic incidents, and
5,161 walk in contacts. Per the request of Jim Parker, Director of Transportation, Public
Safety has worked diligently to provide more patrols and higher visibility. In 2023, PSO’s
contacted over 1,816 staff including bus operators, had 800 in-person citizen contacts,
responded to 64 bus concerns. HOPE had 3,126 contacts with unhoused individuals,
1,268 clean-ups in the community, and 69 unhoused people were placed in housing. In
the CSP division, they handled 180 resident concerns and held 7 Coffee with a
Quadrant Officer events. Lastly, they are making great strides in the Citywide Camera
Installation and have recently installed cameras in Hermosillo, Ramona, and New River
Park. They have plans to continue installations at Vista Verde, Gerdes, and Lakeside
Park, along with Hollifield, Glazier, Zimmerman, Sara Mendes, and Bob White Park in
the near future.

Mr. Ramos introduced the Office of Emergency Management Manager, Richard
Newton, who provided an update on the construction in the EOC and the new
installations. The new updates will be completed soon and will be fully functional to use
for City staff and other government training.

Mr. Ramos introduced the Code Compliance Supervisor, Dolores Bustamante, who
shared that they are responsible for handling the quality-of-life issues in commercial
properties and residential areas. There are four residential inspectors, two commercial
  2
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Norwalk Public Safety Commission
March 4, 2024

inspectors, and two part-time inspectors. They also work with the Community
Development Department who helps with the technical aspect of calls such as zoning
regulations.

Mr. Ramos continued to address vandalism and graffiti within the city. He shared that
the city aims to remove graffiti within 24 hours but with the recent rain, it may take
longer to remove. There has been a significant increase of this at Ramona Park and he
was happy to report that two juveniles were arrested for vandalism and their parents
were held responsible for the fine. The Los Angeles Sheriffs Department has also
arrested individuals involved in a gang and he plans to hold them responsible for
vandalism. The Department has also been focusing on addressing traffic concerns such
as speeding that can cause traffic collisions. They have focused on education,
enforcement, and engineering. He went on to discuss traffic incidents in the city and
verified what intersections had the most accidents last year.

STAFF COMMENTS

Mrs. Orozco went over the March 2024 calendar.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

Commissioner Knieling shared that on Imperial Hwy, by Northgate, there is an individual
who is running the red lights between the hours of 7:30 to 8:00 AM. Additionally, she
has noticed graffiti in Vista Verde Park and believes there were gunshots in the area.
Mr. Ramos said a witness reported a male firing a shot, but no one was injured. Patrols
were increased and he plans to implement a camera and host a Neighborhood Watch
Meeting.

Commissioner Rosoff requested information about the Block Captains, information
about the Parking Plan, and lastly would like statistics and summary of Public Safety.
Mr. Ramos shared the city enacted a Citywide Parking study in 2021, then in 2022 the
council enacted a Parking Action Plan. Phase one has been completed of updating the
municipal code. They have been implementing overnight patrols in quadrant 3 to
analyze the capacity of parking. They are ensuring that all bases are covered by
verifying that residents are using their personal parking spots such as driveways and
looking into different strategies from the report. We have been working to leverage our
Quadrant Officers to build relationships and show our presence. Mr. Ramos expects to
be able to present a robust plan to the City Council to address those concerns. Mr.
Ramos also shared that they are currently working to recruit block captains. Currently,
there are about 30 block captains and aim to have 70 by the end of the year.

Commissioner Fernandez-Silva asked Mrs. Bustamante about the process of inspecting
buildings and the level of cooperation given to inspectors. Mrs. Bustamante shared that
  3

the way inspectors handle inspections depends on a few things such as safety
concerns. When the individual is noncompliant after multiple attempts to gain voluntary
compliance, they can get an inspection warrant. Commissioner Fernandez-Silva shared
his personal experience with inspectors and did not have a pleasant interaction. He
explained that being commissioners helps to have a voice and reduce that stigma of
Code Compliance.

Commissioner Fernandez-Silva also shared his concerns about graffiti, specifically at
Nuffer Elementary and by Alta Med on Rosecrans Ave. Additionally, there has been an
increase of vehicles speeding on and near Sheridan St. by San Antonio Dr. and
Rosecrans Ave.

Commissioner Rodriguez shared that she had recently called her Quadrant Officer Bell,
to discuss a concern she had regarding some neighbors and shared that she
appreciates being able to call someone directly. She also shared her concern about the
new multi-unit housing and the parking issue that may cause. Mr. Ramos explained that
with new buildings, parking is always a factor and they sometimes may do a study to
ensure it is considered. Vice Chair LeGaspi shared that the housing building on
Excelsior Dr. had a beneficial plan of including parking in the lower level to help with
keeping cars on the street to a minimum.

Vice Chair LeGaspi shared his concern about the left turn lane into the shopping center
on Pioneer Blvd. He reports that cars are continuing straight in the left lane and not
turning into the shopping center. He suggested having pylons added onto the lines to
ensure people were turning.

Chair Greenidge expressed her concerns about residences with Christmas lights still on
outside their homes. Mr. Ramos shared that he would work on having a message sent
out to the community to bring awareness of the dangers in keeping lights up.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

There were no persons wishing to address the Public Safety commission.

ADJOURNMENT:

Being no further business to come before the Public Safety Commission, the meeting
was adjourned at 7:03 PM.

  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  April 1, 2024

Chair Greenidge called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. in the Council Chambers,
Norwalk City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to the roll
call were Chair Greenidge, Commissioner Hoskins, Commissioner Knieling, Vice Chair
LeGaspi, Commissioner Pena, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, and Commissioner
Rosoff. Also present were Ozzie Ramos, Director of Public Safety, Berenia Orozco,
Management Analyst, Leslie Peralta, Office Assistant I, Daniel Munoz, Quadrant
Sergeant, and Quadrant Officers Jimmy Gomez and Kimberly Arce.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Chair Greenidge called for the approval of the Public Safety commission meeting
minutes that was held on March 4, 2024. Commissioner Knieling abstained and
requested one revision. Berenia Orozco recorded the revisions and motion to abstain.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Chair Greenidge, Commissioner Hoskins, Vice Chair LeGaspi,
  Commissioner Pena, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Commissioner
  Rosoff
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Commissioner Heard, Commissioner Fernandez-Silva
ABSTAIN: Commissioner Knieling

REPORTS

Mrs. Orozco presented Mr. Ozzie Ramos to give a brief update for the Public Safety
Department. Mr. Ramos gave an overview of the department org chart which displayed
the newly filled vacancies within the department. The department has four trainees that
will soon start employment. Mr. Ramos went on to highlight that many of our employees
that work in the department move on to bigger opportunities and even promote within
the organization. Erica Pena, who was part of our HOPE team, has gone on to work for
the City of Los Angeles Fire Department. Diego Pineda has also joined the Los Angeles
Sheriff’s Department after his time with our HOPE team. Cesar Pineda, who was a
Sergeant for Public Safety has also pursued his dream job as a lineman for the City of
Burbank.

Mr. Ramos went on to speak on the new reports at the I 105 Fwy and Studebaker Rd
concerns. He shared that the area normally has 3-4 traffic accidents a year and this
past year, we unfortunately had 12 traffic accidents. The city has put in a lot of effort to
mediate the issue, where we have reallocated some resources along Studebaker Rd.
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Norwalk Public Safety Commission
April 1, 2024

The priority of these deployments is enforcement, education, and engineering. We are
partnering with Cal Trans, City engineers, and metro to work on this road issue
together. We have deployed message boards advising motorists to slow down as they
exit the freeway. We have met with community members to bring awareness about the
concerns. We have also worked to share incident notifications with our residents.
Enforcement has also played a huge part in our efforts to mediate the situation. We
have also deployed motor deputies to the area to cite speeding motorists.

Mr. Ramos shared that Public Safety partnered with LASD deputies to patrol the area of
Dune St and Studebaker Rd following a tragic incident where a pedestrian was hit.
During this time, about 28 traffic citations were issued and vehicles were impounded.
The main priority during these deployments is to prevent the loss of life for our
pedestrians and motorists.

Sergeant Munoz began sharing that the Quadrant Officer program is a community
partnership team. Quadrant Officer Arce introduced herself as overseeing Quadrant 2
which is anything East of Pioneer and North of Rosecrans. Additionally, Quadrant
Officer Gomez introduced himself as overseeing Quadrant 3 South of Rosecrans and
West of Pioneer. Sergeant Munoz proceeded to introduce the other two Quadrant
Officers that were unable to attend the meeting, which were Officer Bell who oversees
Quadrant 1 North of Rosecrans and West of Pioneer, and Officer Parrales who
oversees Quadrant 4. Sergeant Munoz then explained the way in which the city is split
up, the types of issues Quadrant Officers respond to, and the resources they provide to
businesses and residents in the City. He also gave details on the number of concerns
they’ve responded to and the contacts that they have made with people in the City.

Following Sergeant Munoz’s presentation, Director Ozzie Ramos proceeded to speak to
the commission about the Business Bulletin which was sent out to about 1500
businesses in Norwalk to help build community engagement. This bulletin will be used
to bring awareness about what the Business Watch does, highlight our anchors in
leadership with the Quadrant Officers, and to communicate crime trends.

STAFF COMMENTS

Mrs. Orozco went over the April 2024 calendar.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

Vice Chair LeGaspi communicated his appreciation of all the efforts of the Quadrant
Officer team, and proceeded to inquire about ways that the commission can support the
cadets. Sergeant Munoz invited the commission to speak to the cadets about the
various different career paths that they’ve taken on career day. Vice Chair LeGaspi also
suggested that we collaborate with the Chamber of Commerce to send out the Business
  2

Bulletin electronically. Lastly, he spoke on the issue with vehicles being worked on in
the street, and he inquired who those concerns can be taken to.

Commissioner Rodriguez inquired about the information that Sergeant Munoz
presented, and asked for clarification as to what timeframe that data was collected from.
She also inquired about the Studebaker and 105 Fwy intersection, and whether we can
obtain further data about the collisions happening in this area. Mr. Ramos provided
further details and explained our efforts to be more proactive in addressing this area.

Commissioner Rosoff followed up on a previous request to provide the commission with
“weekly updates” from the Department. He also inquired about the process of holding
parents accountable for any vandalism committed by juveniles such as graffiti. He
wanted to know if any progress had been made and if anyone has been required to pay
restitution yet.

Chair Greenidge expressed her pleasure with the way in which Public Safety Officers
have been addressing graffiti issues in her neighborhood. She mentioned that following
the commission meeting she heard members of the community express gratitude
towards the progress being made.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

There were no persons wishing to address the Public Safety commission.

ADJOURNMENT:

Being no further business to come before the Public Safety Commission, the meeting
was adjourned at 6:39 PM.
